newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Gonzalez may lead OSCE Yugoslavia mission.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Gonzalez may lead OSCE Yugoslavia mission.

text.p: Former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez has been asked to lead a European observer force to investigate disputed local elections in former Yugoslavia, a government spokesman said on Monday.
Gonzalez, now the opposition Socialist party leader, has not yet agreed to lead the mission, an official at party headquarters told Reuters.
"(Prime Minister Jose Maria) Aznar has approved Felipe Gonzalez to lead the delegation," a spokesman for Aznar said.

Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic, under pressure from mass daily street protests over alleged fraud in municipal elections, offered on Friday to allow the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to send a delegation to check the fairness of the poll.

European leaders, meeting in Dublin last week, set conditions for an international team to verify the regularity of last month's elections, including the right to re-run them under international supervision.

Gonzalez lost Spanish elections in March after heading the government for 13 years, discredited by a series of scandals including allegations he masterminded a "dirty war" against the Basque separatist group ETA in which 28 people were killed.
